s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of seizures with altered mental status and history of recent substance use
salient_findings: History of left cerebral ischemic stroke and myocardial infarction 4 months ago
Diffuse bilateral cortical and subcortical edema on brain imaging
key_facts: Presented to the emergency department after a seizure
History of left cerebral ischemic stroke and myocardial infarction 4 months ago
Used synthetic cannabis with resolution of symptoms and neurologic deficits 4 months ago
Used synthetic cannabis just before the seizure
Normal complete blood cell count, chemistry panel, aspirin level, acetaminophen level, alcohol level, and liver function tests
Urine drug screen positive for cannabinoids

shortlist.label: encephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: patient presented with altered mental status and seizures

shortlist.label: ischemic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: patient has a history of left cerebral ischemic stroke and presented with seizures

shortlist.label: encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: patient presented with seizures and altered mental status, and has a history of substance use

shortlist.label: epilepsy
shortlist.why_kept: patient presented with seizures and has no prior seizure disorder

shortlist.label: moyamoya syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: patient has a history of stroke and presented with seizures

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with seizures, altered mental status (Glasgow Coma Scale score of 9), and diffuse bilateral cortical and subcortical edema on imaging studies, in the context of recent synthetic cannabis use, is most consistent with encephalopathy.

rejected.label: ischemic stroke
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of ischemic stroke, the current presentation with seizures and encephalopathy, rather than focal neurologic deficits, makes this less likely.

rejected.label: encephalitis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of fever or infection to support a diagnosis of encephalitis.

rejected.label: epilepsy
rejected.why: The patient has no prior history of seizure disorder, and the seizures in this case are likely secondary to another cause, such as encephalopathy.

rejected.label: moyamoya syndrome
rejected.why: There is no evidence to suggest moyamoya syndrome, such as characteristic imaging findings or a history of recurrent strokes or seizures.
